---
name: technical-writing
description: "Layered technical-writing standard: Diátaxis structure, Google developer style sentences, STE instruction rules, Global English syntax. Use for /technical-writing or when writing or reviewing docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages."
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# Technical writing

The goal is writing a tired engineer understands on the first read. Four layers get you there, one question each: what kind of document is this, how do sentences address the reader, how much does each sentence carry, and can any sentence be read two ways. Apply all four.

Three rules sit above the layers:

- **Cut every word that does no work.** If the sentence survives without a word, the word goes. "In order to" is "to". "It is important to note that" is nothing.
- **Use the short, everyday word.** "Use", not "utilize". "Help", not "facilitate". "Do", not "perform". A long word has to buy its length with precision.
- **When a rule makes a sentence worse, fix the sentence another way or leave it alone.** The rules serve the reader. A sentence that follows every rule and sounds like a machine wrote it has failed.

The codebase is the word list. Write the real symbol, file, flag, or command name, not a synonym or a description of it.

Don't invent jargon. Use the words a developer would say out loud: "move", "delete", "a budget that only decreases", not "evacuate", "ratchet", or "endgame". A named pattern is fine when the doc says what it means the first time. Propose a new offender and its replacement as an addition to `unslop`'s abstract-metaphor rule in your reply, with the diff. Don't edit that skill.

## Vary the rhythm

The layers decide what a document says and how much each sentence carries. A doc can obey all of them and still read machine-written: every sentence clipped short, no view anywhere, nothing specific.

- Mix sentence lengths on purpose. Short sentences land a point. Longer ones that take their time carry a fact with its condition or consequence.
- One thought per sentence does not mean one length per sentence. Split the sentence that carries two thoughts. Keep the long sentence that carries one.
- Have a view where the mode allows it. Explanation weighs trade-offs, so say what you make of them instead of listing pros and cons. Reference stays dry.
- Be specific over sterile. Not "schema changes can cause issues" but "a column rename fails the build".

## Pick the mode first (Diátaxis)

One document, one mode. Two questions pick it: does the content inform action (doing) or understanding (thinking), and does it serve learning or work?

- Action + learning: **tutorial**.
- Action + work: **how-to**.
- Understanding + work: **reference**.
- Understanding + learning: **explanation**.

Use the compass on a whole document or on one sentence.

**Tutorial: learning by doing.** You are the teacher. The learner's success is your job, not theirs. Open by saying what the learner will build, not what they will "learn". Every step produces a visible result, early and often. Tell them what they should see: the expected output, the prompt change, the log line. Cut explanation to one clause and a link. Teaching pauses break the lesson. Stay concrete. Write as "we", in commands: "First, do x. Now, do y."

**How-to: steps to a goal.** Solve a problem a person has, not an operation the machine can perform. Assume competence. Skip teaching. Action only: no digressions, no background, no completeness for its own sake. Link those instead. Allow forks and judgment: "If you want x, do y." Name the guide by the task: "How to calibrate the radar array", not "Radar array calibration".

**Reference: facts for lookup.** Describe. Only describe. No instruction, no persuasion, no opinion. Be dry, complete, and sure. State facts, options, limits, and errors with no hedging. Mirror the structure of the thing described, so code and docs can be navigated together. Put material where readers expect it. Generate from code where possible, so it stays true.

**Explanation: understanding and why.** One bounded topic, readable away from the product. Each title should tolerate an implicit "About..." in front. Anchor on a real why question. Give context: design decisions, history, constraints, alternatives. Opinion is allowed here and nowhere else.

Don't mix modes: no reference tables inside a tutorial, no tutorial hand-holding inside reference, no arguing inside a how-to. Split and link instead.

## Write sentences to the reader (Google developer style)

- Talk to the reader as "you", in the present tense. "Will" only for things that genuinely happen later.
- Say who does what: "the compiler checks", not "is checked". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or beside the point.
- Write instructions as commands: "Click Submit." State facts plainly. Never "should be done".
- Put the condition before the instruction: "To delete the document, click Delete." The reader skips what does not apply.
- Put the common case first. Exceptions after.
- Sound like a knowledgeable friend. No buzzwords, no figurative language, no "please" in instructions, and never "simply", "easy", or "quickly" in a procedure. If it were simple, the reader would not be here.
- Don't pre-announce ("we will soon support...") and don't start consecutive sentences with the same phrase.
- Link with words that say where the link goes: the page title or a short description. Never "click here". Prefer a sentence of context on the page over a link off it.
- Headings carry the point, not just the topic ("Pick the mode first", not "Modes"). Sentence case. A task heading is a bare verb phrase ("Create an instance"). A concept heading is a noun phrase. One h1 per page, no skipped levels.
- Numbered lists for sequences, bullets for everything else. Introduce a list with a complete sentence. Keep items parallel.
- Code goes in code font. UI elements go in bold. Use serial commas. Drop "etc." and say up front that a list is partial.

## Make statements load one at a time (STE rules)

- One instruction per sentence. One thought per sentence everywhere else.
- Split instructions longer than about 20 words and other sentences longer than about 25.
- Put the warning or condition before the step it guards: "If hot oil touches your skin, injuries can occur."
- Keep "the" and "a": "Remove backup file" reads two ways. "Remove the backup file" reads one.
- Give each word one meaning and one job, then keep it. If "check" means inspect, don't also use it for restrain.
- Pick one word per action and stick to it: "start", not "start" here and "initiate" there.
- Write procedures as direct commands, never as narration and never in the passive: "Install the component", not "the component must be installed".
- Avoid "-ing" words where you can. They take too many grammatical jobs and breed misreadings.

## Leave no sentence open to two readings (Global English)

- Keep words like "only" and "not" next to the word they change: "only fails on growth" and "fails only on growth" say different things.
- Break up long noun strings: "the proto import budget check script" becomes "the script that checks the proto-import budget".
- Make every "it", "they", and "this" point at one obvious thing. Repeat the noun when in doubt. Never use "this" or "which" to point at a whole clause.
- Don't drop verbs: "Phase 1 moves the converters and Phase 2 the runtime" leaves Phase 2 without one. Give it one.
- Keep the small words that show structure. "Ensure that the switch is off" keeps "that" because it makes the sentence parse one way. Never trade clarity for word count.
- Repeat the article in a series when it prevents a misread: "the client and the host", not "the client and host", when they are two things.
- Say which parts "and" or "or" joins when a sentence can group two ways. "Both...and", "either...or", and "if...then" are free disambiguators.
- Use periods, not semicolons. Replace an em dash with a new sentence.
- Make text in parentheses a full grammatical unit or its own sentence. Never form plurals with "(s)".
- No slashes: write "a, b, or both" instead of "a/b" or "and/or".
- Call each thing by one name, everywhere. A doc that says "the gate", "the ratchet", and "the budget check" for one thing teaches three things. Rewording an unchanged sentence between edits costs the same way. Don't churn what didn't change.
- Skip idioms, colloquialisms, Latin abbreviations, and metaphors. A non-native reader, a translator, and an agent all parse plain constructions best.

## Voice and repo specifics

- Apply the **unslop** skill to every doc this skill touches. That skill owns the slop-pattern catalog: AI vocabulary, filler, hedging, formatting tells.
- PR descriptions and commit messages are writing too. Every layer except Diátaxis applies to them. A PR body is a briefing that a reviewer can read in under a minute. Do not paste swarm logs, SHA lists, or metric tables. Link them.
- Product UI strings are not documentation. Use your product's copy guidelines for those.
- Indent code snippets with tabs. Write real paths and real symbols. Make every count or tree claim true at the commit that lands it, and include the command that regenerates it.

## Worked example

Before:

> Configuration of the proto import ratchet budget script parameters is performed via budget.json. Note that it's important to remember that running with --write, which updates the committed budget to reflect the current count, should only be done when lowering it. If exceeded, CI fails.

After:

> `budget.mjs` reads the committed budget from `budget.json` and counts the files that import protos. If the count exceeds the budget, CI fails. Run `budget.mjs --write` only to lower the budget.
---
name: principle-prove-it-works
description: "Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'"
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# Prove It Works

Verify every task output by checking the real thing directly. Do not infer from proxies, self-reports, or "it compiles."

**Why:** Unverified work has unknown correctness. Indirect verification (file mtimes, output freshness, agent self-reports, cached screenshots) feels cheaper than direct observation. Acting on a wrong inference costs far more than checking the source.

Check the real thing, not a proxy:
- Check process liveness directly, not indirectly through derived state
- Read the actual value, not a cached or derived representation
- When verification fails, suspect the observation method before suspecting the system

## Script the check when you can

The strongest proof is a deterministic script that re-runs the same comparison, not a one-time eyeball. Write the script, run it, and keep its output as an artifact a reviewer can re-run instead of trusting your word.

Keep the artifact visible for the human. Commit it only for large or complex work where the trail has to be auditable later, like a big port or migration (the **show-me-your-work** skill).
---
name: principle-build-the-lever
description: "Apply to any non-trivial work, not just bulk work: edits, migrations, analyses, checks. Build the tool that does it or proves it (codemod, script, generator, or a skill your subagents follow) instead of working by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun."
disable-model-invocation: true
---
# Build the Lever

When the work isn't trivial, build the tool that does it instead of doing it by hand.

**Why:** Two payoffs. Throughput: a codemod, generator, or script does the work the same way every time and reruns for free. Confidence: the tool is one artifact a reviewer can read and rerun to check the work. Hand-done changes can only be re-verified by redoing them. A deterministic script turns "trust me" into "run this".

**Pattern:** Default to building the lever. Skip it only when the task is trivial, a couple of obvious edits you can see at a glance.

- Do the first unit by hand to learn the recipe, then build the tool. Prove it by rerunning it on that unit and diffing against your hand-done version. Make the lever safe to rerun.
- Codemod or script for edits, generator for repetitive files, a dump-to-sqlite query for analysis, a rerunnable check for verification.
- A deterministic lever beats fan-out. If the tool can process every unit in one pass, run it yourself. Don't fan out delegates to hand-apply what a script can do.
- When you fan work out to subagents, write the lever as a skill they all read: the recipe, the verification contract, and the do-not-touch fences in one artifact. Keep it outside the delegates' write scope so they can't quietly edit the contract.
- Applying this principle produces a file. If you cited it and there is no codemod, script, generator, or delegate skill in the diff, you didn't apply it.
- Commit the lever when the work outlives the session.

**Balance:** The bar is triviality, not repetition. A one-off still earns a lever when the lever is what makes the work checkable. Per the [Laziness Protocol](../principle-laziness-protocol/SKILL.md), build the smallest script that does or proves the job, never a framework.

Distinct from [Encode Lessons in Structure](../principle-encode-lessons-in-structure/SKILL.md), which makes a recurring instruction a durable guardrail. This is throughput and reviewability on the work in front of you. For scripting the verification itself, see [Prove It Works](../principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md).

TOPO selection is optional. Eligible nearby surveyed covers support manholes. TOPO never becomes the original baseline reference. Generic nodes can affect missing-data counts but do not enter geometry-deviation review.

## Distance and decisions

Manhole distance uses centroids. Alignment distance is the maximum offset of final vertices from the original geometry. This is not a symmetric Hausdorff distance. A shorter final line lying on the original can have zero offset.

The rule comes from **DIR_DEVIATION** for **R3_2026**. The documented threshold is 600 mm. The code reads the rule at runtime; this run did not query its live value.

- **Within tolerance** is confirmed automatically.
- Certain polygon manhole matches are confirmed automatically even when deviated. They use matching infrastructure keys or strict spatial overlap.
- Other deviations remain pending. Review requires a measured distance, a matching outcome, and a correction flag for a deviation.
- The reviewer can explicitly set a new original reference. Selecting a feature alone does not save it.
- **No baseline match** sends a rejected outcome with no distance or correction. It clears the original reference, preserves a reviewed audit row, and updates missing-data counts. It creates no Grade E geometry.

Unmatched final manholes remain pending for review. Unmatched alignments and original-only features are summary counts, not new geometry findings. A rejected manhole counts as Found Additional in the report; rejected alignments do not enter its summary.

See [[Compile and exports]] for the Grade E boundary. Earlier saved analysis methods keep their older behavior until sources reset the analysis.

Each review stays anchored to a final GeoCUP feature. Matching first uses compatible kind and infrastructure keys, then a compatible baseline within 10 m. A manhole can also match one uncoded polygon with strict full-overlap conditions.

TOPO selection is optional. Eligible nearby surveyed covers support manholes. TOPO never becomes the original baseline reference. Generic nodes can affect missing-data counts but do not enter geometry-deviation review.

## Distance and decisions

Manhole distance uses centroids. Alignment distance is the maximum offset of final vertices from the original geometry. This is not a symmetric Hausdorff distance. A shorter final line lying on the original can have zero offset.

The rule comes from **DIR_DEVIATION** for **R3_2026**. The documented threshold is 600 mm. The code reads the rule at runtime; this run did not query its live value.

- **Within tolerance** is confirmed automatically.
- Certain polygon manhole matches are confirmed automatically even when deviated. They use matching infrastructure keys or strict spatial overlap.
- Other deviations remain pending. Review requires a measured distance, a matching outcome, and a correction flag for a deviation.
- The reviewer can explicitly set a new original reference. Selecting a feature alone does not save it.
- **No baseline match** sends a rejected outcome with no distance or correction. It clears the original reference, preserves a reviewed audit row, and updates missing-data counts. It creates no Grade E geometry.

Unmatched final manholes remain pending for review. Unmatched alignments and original-only features are summary counts, not new geometry findings. A rejected manhole counts as Found Additional in the report; rejected alignments do not enter its summary.

See [[Compile and exports]] for the Grade E boundary. Earlier saved analysis methods keep their older behavior until sources reset the analysis.

Each review stays anchored to a final GeoCUP feature. Matching first uses compatible kind and infrastructure keys, then a compatible baseline within 10 m. A manhole can also match one uncoded polygon with strict full-overlap conditions.

TOPO selection is optional. Eligible nearby surveyed covers support manholes. TOPO never becomes the original baseline reference. Generic nodes can affect missing-data counts but do not enter geometry-deviation review.

## Distance and decisions

Manhole distance uses centroids. Alignment distance is the maximum offset of final vertices from the original geometry. This is not a symmetric Hausdorff distance. A shorter final line lying on the original can have zero offset.

The rule comes from **DIR_DEVIATION** for **R3_2026**. The documented threshold is 600 mm. The code reads the rule at runtime; this run did not query its live value.

- **Within tolerance** is confirmed automatically.
- Certain polygon manhole matches are confirmed automatically even when deviated. They use matching infrastructure keys or strict spatial overlap.
- Other deviations remain pending. Review requires a measured distance, a matching outcome, and a correction flag for a deviation.
- The reviewer can explicitly set a new original reference. Selecting a feature alone does not save it.
- **No baseline match** sends a rejected outcome with no distance or correction. It clears the original reference, preserves a reviewed audit row, and updates missing-data counts. It creates no Grade E geometry.

Unmatched final manholes remain pending for review. Unmatched alignments and original-only features are summary counts, not new geometry findings. A rejected manhole counts as Found Additional in the report; rejected alignments do not enter its summary.

See [[Compile and exports]] for the Grade E boundary. Earlier saved analysis methods keep their older behavior until sources reset the analysis.

It also requires an original baseline category and version. The server resolves every matching layer in that baseline group. Eligible baseline categories are **S5A_CUP** and **S5_GCUP**.

The reviewer must confirm original provenance. The baseline group must not contain any selected final layer. A same-version independent import discussed in older plans can therefore still be rejected when the resolved category/version group contains the final import.

## Working area

# DIR six-stage workflow review and refactor plan

Status: implemented as workflow version 3. The original plan and template review remain below.

Update 2026-10-21: Baseline setup now selects a category and version. It includes all matching project layers and rejects a group containing the selected final GeoCUP import. See `docs/specs/dir-automation.md` for the current API.

## Template review

Source: [GIS Templates (Annex C Aug 2026 Release)](../../reference/testing/GIS%20Templates%20%28Annex%20C%20Aug%202026%20Release%29.pdf), PDF pages 95–102.

- Page 96, template Step 2, overlays the **whole topographic survey** with the CUP for surface structures “such as manhole covers.” Manholes are an example of survey evidence. The page's explicit Grade B and 600 mm Grade E rules, however, are stated for surveyed manhole locations and corresponding **CUP manhole records**. They must not automatically be applied to every TOPO feature.
- Page 97, template Step 3, uses the Step 2 survey locations to adjust CUP alignments and consolidate multiple covers of one manhole. It does not request a second TOPO selection. It compares **original service-plan alignments** with the adjusted alignments for the 600 mm Grade E decision. That original geometry remains necessary for a template DIR.
- Pages 98–99, template Steps 4 and 4A, can share one investigation stage. Whole-segment grading uses non-invasive evidence and may also use TTR evidence. Page 100 adds TTR, so B+ and any TTR-dependent whole-segment grade must be finalized after the TTR stage.
- Pages 101–102 define final graded GeoCUP and mandatory compilation of inaccurate legacy Grade E geometry into DIR.

The proposed six UI stages are feasible as a **product workflow**, but their labels are not a one-to-one restatement of the template. “Compare GeoCUP with TOPO” is an audit of the already selected final GeoCUP. Template Grade E requires the corresponding original CUP/service-plan geometry; a mismatch between GeoCUP and TOPO alone is not enough to create DIR geometry.

## Recommended six stages

| New UI stage | Template work retained | Inputs and result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Review GeoCUP | Current final-data grade summary and template Step 1 baseline | Review every feature's stored grade in the fixed `S5_GCUP` dataset. Show missing grades and alignment totals. Record any service-plan Grade D defaults only against an identified CUP/service-plan baseline; never assign D to ungraded final GeoCUP by assumption. |
| 2. Review TOPO and adjust alignments | Template Steps 2 + 3 | Select one or more complete `S1_TOPO` datasets by version once. Load all their layers. Run separate surface-structure and alignment subchecks using the same survey selection. Review cover consolidation, surveyed Grade B evidence, adjusted alignment proposals, and the 600 mm rules only where their source and feature roles support them. |
| 3. Review EML/MCGPR and coverage | Template Steps 4 + 4A | Select complete `S2_EML` and/or `S3_MCGPR` datasets. Compare their evidence with the fixed GeoCUP and original CUP geometry. Measure validated segment lengths and propose C+, B-, B, or provisional B. Retain the coverage basis and review decision. |
| 4. Review Trial Trench | Template Step 5 and final 4A result | Select complete `S4_TTR` datasets. Review positive verification and grade changes. Recalculate affected whole-segment grades after TTR; B+ requires full non-invasive coverage plus local TTR evidence. |
| 5. Validate final GeoCUP | Template Step 6 | Check every final GeoCUP alignment has an appropriate grade and reconcile reviewed evidence. Do not overwrite uploaded geometry or grades. |
| 6. Compile DIR and report | Template Step 7 | Mandatory. Compile only reviewed Grade E **legacy** geometry; generate provenance and owner summaries. Record skipped checks, including missing CUP/source evidence. |

Stages 1–5 may be skipped with a reason if that remains the user's policy. Stage 6 remains mandatory. A skipped or unavailable baseline never produces inferred Grade E records. An all-skipped study produces an empty DIR with an explicit no-assessment statement.

## Source selection and semantic authority

1. Freeze exactly one final `S5_GCUP` dataset at study creation, as today. The UI can display its category and version.
2. Expose an evidence-dataset projection grouped by **category, stable `source_dataset_id`, and version**. Each choice contains its complete layer ID set. For older rows without an import ID, use conservative source/time grouping; do not merge unrelated uploads solely because they share a version. Show category and version in the picker, with a short disambiguator only when needed.
3. Stage 2 selects whole `S1_TOPO` datasets, never individual TOPO layers. Its two subchecks reuse exactly that frozen selection. Use the same dataset-level picker pattern for EML/MCGPR and TTR.
4. Preserve source roles in the backend: final GeoCUP, original CUP/service plan, TOPO surface evidence, EML/MCGPR, and TTR. Feature classification and grading rules remain backend projections. The frontend renders choices and findings; it does not infer engineering rules from layer names or geometry alone.
5. **Confirmed baseline choice:** select one original baseline dataset at study setup and reuse it in Stages 1–4. The baseline may be CUP/service-plan data or a distinct `S5_GCUP` dataset, including one with the same version number as the final GeoCUP, if it represents original geometry. Version number and upload time alone do not establish that role. Record the user's source-provenance confirmation. The exact same imported dataset cannot be both the baseline and final GeoCUP for a DIR comparison: a self-comparison cannot identify inaccurate legacy geometry. When only that dataset exists, permit grade review and evidence checks, but block Grade E compilation and state the missing independent baseline in the report.

## Incremental implementation plan

1. Add workflow version 3 with six stage states and stable subcheck identifiers. Keep version 2 studies and their reports readable; do not reinterpret old step numbers. Add versioned API behavior or additive routes so existing API clients retain their contracts.
2. Add the backend dataset projection for TOPO, EML, MCGPR, TTR, CUP/service-plan, and eligible GeoCUP baseline data. Validate complete dataset membership, project ownership, category, source hashes, and duplicate selections. Do not impose an older-version requirement on the baseline; reject the identical final dataset for DIR geometry comparison.
3. Move the current GeoCUP grade summary into Stage 1. If the baseline has verified data-owner service-plan provenance, reuse its reviewed Grade D defaults without modifying source data. A `S5_GCUP` category or same version is not proof of service-plan provenance. Keep final GeoCUP missing grades separate.
4. Combine template Steps 2 and 3 in Stage 2 with two recorded subchecks. Survey all selected TOPO layers, but apply the explicit manhole 600 mm rule only to reviewed manhole matches. Reuse TOPO evidence for adjusted alignment proposals. Compare original service-plan geometry with the accepted adjustment before a Grade E proposal. Preserve one-to-many cover links and reviewer overrides.
5. Combine template Steps 4 and 4A in Stage 3. Store proposed and confirmed coverage separately. Stage 4 incorporates TTR evidence and revises only dependent grade decisions; it must not silently change accepted findings. Reopening an earlier stage invalidates affected downstream reviews.
6. Keep Stage 5 as final GeoCUP grade validation and Stage 6 as mandatory compilation. Update the workbook to show six stages, underlying template checks, selected dataset versions, reviewer decisions, coverage, source geometry links, and skipped checks. Generate DIR_CLIN/DIR_NODE only from confirmed legacy Grade E records.
7. Update the settings UI to show six stages and dataset-level version pickers. Present the Stage 2 surface and alignment subchecks separately within one stage. Keep old version 2 studies accessible under previous workflows.
8. Test older and same-version independent baseline imports, identical-dataset rejection for Grade E, full TOPO dataset selection, non-manhole TOPO context without false Grade E, one survey selection reused by both subchecks, multiple covers per manhole, 599/600 mm boundaries, baseline/adjusted alignment provenance, 4A coverage thresholds, TTR-dependent B+, skip behavior, final grade validation, DIR geometry/report output, and version 2 compatibility.

The baseline-source choice is agreed. The implementation must preserve the independent-source check and explicit provenance confirmation.
# DIR Stage 2: GeoCUP anchored comparison

Status: implemented for new Stage 2 analyses. Saved older analyses remain available until the user resets Stage 2.

## Template check

The source is `reference/testing/GIS Templates (Annex C Aug 2026 Release).pdf`, printed pages 96–97.

- Page 96, Step 2: overlay the topographic survey with the CUP from Step 1. Use surveyed surface structures, especially manhole covers, to verify corresponding CUP manhole locations. A surveyed manhole location supports Grade B. A difference of at least 600 mm marks the **CUP manhole record** Grade E.
- Page 97, Step 3: adjust CUP alignments to the actual manhole locations. Such a logical alignment adjustment is Grade C. Compare the **original service plan alignment** with the adjusted alignment; a difference of at least 600 mm marks the original alignment Grade E. Correlate multiple covers with one manhole using the service plan.
- These pages describe the template's CUP construction sequence. The DIR application receives an already graded final GeoCUP. Using that GeoCUP as the Stage 2 anchor is the proposed product mapping, not a literal statement on pages 96–97. Keep the final uploaded geometry and grade as source data; record the template check and its evidence separately.

## Current behavior and findings

- `app/services/dir_workflow_v3.py:423-461` indexes final GeoCUP, but iterates **original baseline** manholes, alignments, and generic nodes. It writes a `DirFinding` for every original feature even when `match` is absent. It only adds unmatched final manholes if a TOPO point is nearby.
- The inspected Stage 2 study `f6c0ff5c-9439-4557-8921-edbffe846fc3` has 40,964 records: 38,098 original-only records, 2,866 records with original and final features, and zero final-only records. Kind counts are 21,866 alignments, 19,098 generic nodes, and zero manholes. These are read-only database counts from 21 October 2026. This is a direct result of the baseline-driven loop, not evidence that 38,098 original features need correction.
- For generic nodes, `_stage_two_nearby(..., "all", 2, None)` attaches the two nearest TOPO features with no maximum distance or surface-structure check. This can make a baseline-only review record appear to contain TOPO evidence. A TOPO feature alone never creates a record in this code; a preview with TOPO and no original is the final-only manhole path.
- For alignments, the code measures original against matched GeoCUP using Hausdorff distance, but it also requires nearby TOPO **points** for a reviewer to confirm a deviation. TOPO lines are ignored by that alignment evidence search. For manholes, it measures original against the nearest TOPO point, not against final GeoCUP. Both checks are mixed into one outcome model.
- The current study has no manhole findings. The selected final data contains no point features and the selected TOPO data contains no point features, so the page 96 manhole-cover rule cannot be checked from those selections. Do not infer manhole evidence from a generic line or node.
- `review()` allows `not_found` on an original-only alignment or manhole. `generate_dir()` can then copy that original geometry into Grade E DIR without a final GeoCUP match. The report also counts original-only findings as studied. This is the downstream reason the wrong candidate set matters.
- The UI loads the whole findings array and offers editable GeoCUP and evidence IDs. It does not show separate page 96 and page 97 checks. The source loading and per-record review become expensive with the current 40,964-record candidate set.

## Proposed behavior

1. Keep the selected final graded GeoCUP as the fixed comparison anchor. Build one candidate group per eligible final manhole or final alignment inside the study area. Original and TOPO data are linked evidence. Do not make TOPO-only review records. Run a separate missing-data check **only between final GeoCUP and the original service plan**, in both directions. Show unmatched final and unmatched original counts there; do not count unmatched TOPO or turn a missing-data count into Grade E automatically.
2. Make separate manhole and alignment comparison kinds. Exclude generic nodes from Grade E review. Classify survey cover points from source attributes and geometry; use a source-specific rule, not all TOPO points. If no eligible survey cover exists, keep the GeoCUP-to-original manhole comparison without a missing-TOPO review item or summary count.
3. For each final manhole, find corresponding original manhole and surveyed cover or cover group by stable ID, owner/type, and bounded spatial search. Preserve one-to-many cover links. Present the exact pair, distance, and evidence for review. Apply the 600 mm Grade E rule only to the original manhole after a reviewer confirms the correspondence and measured distance. The final GeoCUP grade remains unchanged.
4. For each final alignment, find the corresponding original alignment and any related reviewed manhole/TOPO evidence. Compare original geometry with the accepted adjusted final alignment. Record the distance method and the TOPO basis when available. Apply the 600 mm Grade E rule only to the original alignment after a reviewer confirms the match and adjustment. Do not require TOPO point geometry when the alignment evidence is a surveyed line or a reviewed manhole connection.
5. Treat unmatched final and unmatched original features as results of the GeoCUP-to-original missing-data check. Show their counts in that check, separate from geometry-deviation reviews. Do not create a missing-TOPO status, item, or count. The new method does not offer `not_found` as a geometry-review outcome.
6. Store the method version and missing-data counts in Stage 2 state. Use the finding kind for manhole and alignment checks, `new_feature_ids[0]` for the fixed final anchor, and `evidence_feature_ids` for optional cover links. Require a valid final anchor and an original feature for a Grade E decision. Lock the anchor against replacement during review. Keep source IDs for traceability.
7. Update the Stage 2 UI to show the final GeoCUP first, then original and available TOPO evidence, in separate manhole and alignment queues. Show missing-data results only for GeoCUP versus original. Page findings instead of loading the whole array. Update workbook counts to use only reviewed, valid final-anchored comparisons; report unmatched GeoCUP and original counts separately.
8. Preserve existing study findings and generated outputs as historical data. Use an analysis method version for new Stage 2 runs. Reanalysis must explicitly replace the Stage 2 findings for that study and invalidate dependent review/output; it must not silently reinterpret saved reviewer decisions.

## Checks before release

- Confirm that geometry-deviation review records have a final GeoCUP anchor. Confirm that missing-data results include only unmatched GeoCUP and original features.
- Check real data with absent cover points and final manholes: retain GeoCUP-to-original manhole comparisons and create no missing-TOPO item or count.
- Check one manhole with several covers, a cover that is far away, and owner/type conflicts.
- Check 599 mm and 600 mm manhole and alignment differences, missing original data, true site absence, and final geometry without survey evidence. The last case must create no missing-TOPO item or count.
- Confirm that Grade E output copies only the reviewed original geometry and that final grades do not change.
- Check report counts, reopening behavior, and response time on the inspected 40,964-record study.

## Confirmed missing-data scope

Missing data is checked only between the latest graded GeoCUP and original service plan. Missing TOPO data is neither reviewed nor listed in the missing-data summary.
# DIR automation

The original DIR workflow compares two selected GeoCUP versions. Workflow version 2 follows Annex C August 2026 pages 95–102 with one fixed highest-version GeoCUP import and separate source choices for each step. Workflow version 3 groups the review into six stages. Uploaded data remains unchanged.

Version 3 selects one highest-version `S5_GCUP` import and one confirmed original baseline category and version at setup. The baseline can be `S5A_CUP` or `S5_GCUP`. Every project layer with that exact category and version becomes a baseline layer, including layers from separate imports. Setup rejects a baseline group containing the selected final GeoCUP import. Existing studies retain their stored layer selection. Stage 1 reviews final GeoCUP grades and may assign study-local Grade D defaults only to ungraded records from a distinct baseline confirmed as data-owner service-plan data. Stage 2 selects whole `S1_TOPO` imports once for surface and alignment review. Other surface records can be reviewed against TOPO evidence, but the manhole distance rule does not grade them or create Grade E geometry. Stage 3 selects whole `S2_EML` and `S3_MCGPR` imports for investigation and coverage. Stage 4 selects whole `S4_TTR` imports and finalizes TTR-dependent grades. Stage 5 audits final GeoCUP grades and records missing alignment grades without changing source data. Stages 1–5 can be skipped with a reason. Stage 6 compiles DIR and the report and cannot be skipped. The report records source imports, stage states, grade counts, reviewed evidence, and each ungraded final alignment after Stage 5 completes. Version 2 studies remain accessible under Previous DIR studies.

Version 3 uses additive `/api/v1/projects/{project_id}/dir/v3/workflows` routes for create, source selection, stage analysis, review, skip, compile, and delete. `eligible-layers` now projects whole source datasets and version 3 stage requirements. The existing report download and GIS export routes remain in use.

Stage 2 uses two linked map canvases. The left canvas shows the fixed blue GeoCUP review feature and only the selected baseline in gray. The right canvas retains colored candidates and survey evidence. Current Stage 2 baseline context and reference-choice responses include optional `measurement_geometry`, a two-endpoint GeoJSON LineString in EPSG:3414. Its endpoints connect manhole centroids, or the final alignment vertex with the largest offset to its nearest baseline point. The left canvas draws this measurement as a dark dotted line with a midpoint label rounded to three decimal places in metres. Coincident endpoints retain a `0.000 m` label. Selecting GeoCUP or survey evidence clears the gray overlay and measurement. Selection does not save a reference or change reviews. Context baseline distances use this Stage 2 rule; survey distances retain the shortest geometry gap. Historical comparisons without measurement data retain feature inspection without a connector. No database migration is required.

Grade summaries show a compact table with Lines (alignments), Points, Polygons, and Manholes as rows and Total, Ungraded, A, B, C, D as columns. A Features footer shows the overall counts. Zero counts remain visible. Other source grades, such as B+ or E, appear as extra columns when present. The table scrolls horizontally on narrow screens. An information icon beside Manholes opens a tooltip on hover, focus, or tap, explaining the `MHOL`, `MH--`, and `MHST` feature codes, space and case handling, and the point or polygon requirement. Manholes count separately from other points and polygons. Every feature counts once. All line features remain in Lines. The grade-summary API adds `feature_types`, with `total`, `missing`, and `grades` for each group; existing summary fields remain available. Older saved Stage 1 reviews use the live final summary for this display when their saved summary has no feature breakdown.

Stages 2–4 can read `GET /dir/v3/workflows/{id}/stages/{code}/findings/{finding_id}/context`. It returns the backend-selected review feature, the finding's paired original baseline feature when present, and features from that stage's baseline, final GeoCUP, and evidence layers whose stored geometries touch or intersect the review feature exactly. The paired baseline feature is included even when it does not intersect the review feature. Each geometry has a feature ID, source layer, role, and shortest geometry distance to the review feature in metres. The DIR viewer highlights the review feature and reads clicked feature attributes from the existing project feature-attributes API. IPAG field metadata comes from the layer semantics API when available. This view does not change reviews or source data.

Stage 2 context also includes explicitly linked survey evidence, even when it does not intersect the review feature. Stage 2 reference choices return their stored EPSG:3414 `geometry`. The viewer uses two linked north-up Mapbox canvases, with the review feature on the left and candidates and evidence on the right. Stored EPSG:3414 coordinates are projected to WGS84 for display. The Mapbox Light basemap starts at 40% opacity, with a slider to adjust it independently of the feature overlays. Native drag, wheel, double-click, and touch navigation are enabled, with zoom buttons, a metric scale, Fit all, and Focus selected controls. Each baseline candidate has its own color, matched to the compact candidate panel on the right. Candidate colors stay stable while searching and changing the original reference within a finding. The latest graded GeoCUP layer uses fixed blue (`#2563eb`) on the map and its card, including the review feature and other final features. Its card stays pinned above the right panel’s scrolling candidate contents. Inspecting or changing a baseline reference does not replace this review anchor. The original reference is identified in the panel and outlined on the map; it keeps its candidate color. The right panel can be resized with its divider, using pointer drag or the arrow keys. Double-click resets its width to 290 px. The width is limited to 240–560 px and leaves at least 320 px for the map; Mapbox resizes with the layout. On small screens, the scrollable candidate panel moves below the map and the divider is hidden. Stage 2 also has Hide findings/Show findings controls for the left findings panel. When hidden, a compact selector keeps finding navigation available and the current review draft stays intact. Stage 2 uses 12 px page side padding, a narrower findings panel, and smaller column gaps to give the map more width. Inspection and map navigation remain available for generated studies while review edits stay locked. Clicking or keyboard-selecting a feature shows its distance to the review feature. Eligible candidates have a **Set as original reference** button below the map; selection alone does not save a change. Baseline candidate distances use the same Stage 2 rule as reference changes: centroid distance for manholes, or maximum final-vertex offset from the baseline for alignments. These distances override the context's shortest geometry distance, including for intersecting candidates. The default choice list includes the nearest 30 candidates and all intersecting candidates; ID search finds other eligible baseline features. Search results appear on the same map.

For current Stage 2 GeoCUP anchored comparisons, automatic matching first uses the same feature kind and infrastructure key (owner, infrastructure type, feature type, infrastructure ID), then the nearest compatible baseline geometry within 10 m. If a final manhole has no typed baseline match, one uncoded baseline polygon may match automatically only when both geometries are valid, their intersection covers at least 90% of their combined area, their centroids are within the DIR tolerance, and known owner and infrastructure type values agree. Multiple qualifying polygons prevent automatic selection. Otherwise the final manhole becomes a pending, unverified finding instead of disappearing from review. Selected TOPO points coded `MH`, `MHOL`, `MH--`, or `MHST` can appear as nearby survey evidence. TOPO evidence does not become the original baseline reference. The reviewer can confirm no baseline match or select a reference from the study's original baseline. Reference choices include same-kind features and uncoded baseline polygons for manholes. The choices include the nearest 30 results and every eligible baseline feature intersecting the review feature, even when a search term is present. The viewer places the review feature and baseline reference first, then lists connected features and baseline choices. Clicking a feature opens its attributes; eligible baseline rows can set the reference. `PATCH /stages/2/findings/{finding_id}/reference` selects one baseline feature with a finding revision check. The server rejects a feature outside the study baseline or an ineligible type. A baseline feature may reference more than one final GeoCUP feature, as automatic typed matching already permits. The server recalculates the geometric distance and applies the deviation rule without changing the final GeoCUP review feature. Polygon manholes with matching infrastructure keys or full spatial overlap are automatically confirmed, including deviations. Comparisons within tolerance are also automatically confirmed. Other deviations remain pending for review. Stage 2 completes when no findings remain pending.

`GET /dir/eligible-layers` returns `baseline_groups`, with one category and version choice plus layer count per group. The version 3 baseline picker uses `baseline_groups`; `source_datasets` and `source_layers` remain for import and older step choices. Version 3 setup accepts `baseline_category`, `baseline_version`, and `baseline_is_original`; it resolves all matching project layers on the server. The older `baseline_dataset_key` request field remains accepted for existing clients and resolves its import key to the full category and version group. New study responses include `baseline_category`. Apply migration `f2d7a8c3e915` before using this setup contract.

Version 3 setup accepts `working_area`: `{"mode":"whole"}`, `{"mode":"boundary_layer","layer_ids":[...]}`, `{"mode":"project_boundary"}`, or `{"mode":"drawn_box","bbox":[[lng1,lat1],[lng2,lat2]]}`. The drawn box accepts either corner order. The boundary layer choice takes exactly one polygon layer registered as a project boundary. The server checks this association again when it creates a study. `eligible-layers` returns only registered polygon layers in `working_area_boundary_layers`. The older `topo_layers` mode remains readable for existing studies and clients. Drawn box coordinates use WGS84 longitude and latitude. New `whole` studies save the union of a 10 metre buffer around every selected final GeoCUP feature. Each feature is buffered before polygon unions are merged in batches of 64, avoiding the large intermediate line network created by merging lines first. This limits baseline and evidence analysis to the area covered by final GeoCUP. Existing studies with no saved area retain their original full dataset scope. The database choice uses `project.boundary_box`. Each selected area is saved with the study in EPSG:3414. Features that touch it stay whole for grade counts, evidence, findings, DIR geometry, and report lengths. Selected source imports still include all their layers; no uploaded feature is clipped or changed. The study response returns its area mode and selected layer IDs. Apply migration `e1c5f7a2b904` before using these setup choices.

The web DIR setup shows Working area below the GeoCUP and baseline selectors. It offers latest GeoCUP area, a registered project boundary layer, the stored project boundary box, and a drawn box. It disables the layer choice when the project has no registered boundary layer. It sends the selection when the user starts a new study. A saved study shows its area but cannot change it.

The web DIR page shows a new study as a setup form (`DirStudySetup`) and a saved study as a read-only "Study sources" summary bar (`DirStudySummary`) with the Delete workflow button. The final and baseline grade tables are in Stage 1. At 1280 px and wider, the stage bar and the finding list stay in view while the geometry preview and the decision form sit side by side. Narrower screens keep the stage and finding select lists.

New version 3 Stage 2 analyses anchor each geometry review to a final GeoCUP manhole or alignment matched with an original service-plan feature. Manhole distance compares geometry centroids. Alignment distance is the maximum distance from final alignment vertices to the original geometry, so a shorter final alignment that lies on a longer original alignment has near-zero deviation. TOPO selection is optional. Eligible surveyed TOPO covers can support a manhole check as evidence, but a missing cover does not remove the GeoCUP-to-original comparison. Original-to-TOPO distance is not the proposed deviation. Missing TOPO features create no review item or summary count. A separate missing-data summary counts original features absent from GeoCUP and GeoCUP features absent from original service plans. Generic nodes do not enter geometry-deviation review. The UI fixes the final GeoCUP anchor, shows the paired original and any TOPO evidence, and reports only the two GeoCUP-to-original missing-data counts. The Stage 2 findings endpoint accepts optional `offset` and `limit` query values, and the UI loads 100 findings per page. Reviewers confirm distances and outcomes; a confirmed deviation of at least 600 mm can add the original geometry to Grade E DIR. Uploaded GeoCUP geometry and grade stay unchanged. Existing Stage 2 analyses keep their saved method and findings; changing sources starts a new analysis and clears dependent reviews.

For current version 3 Stage 2 GeoCUP anchored comparisons, the "No baseline match" action sends `outcome: "rejected"` with no distance or correction. It clears the proposed original reference, counts the GeoCUP feature as unmatched, and counts the original feature as unmatched if no other comparison uses it. The finding stays reviewed and visible for audit, with a blank original feature ID and "No baseline match" outcome in the workbook. It does not enter Grade E output. Reviewed manholes without a baseline count as Found Additional and correction in the page 103 report; rejected alignments remain outside the summary. Selecting a new original reference later restores a paired comparison and updates both missing-data counts. Earlier Stage 2 analysis methods retain their existing rejection behavior.

## Template workflow (version 2)

Migration `b7e2c5d9a401` adds import identity, step state, and step-linked findings. Migration `c8f3d6e0b512` stores proposed coverage separately from confirmed coverage. New imports share one `source_dataset_id` across their stored layers. DIR groups these layers by category, version, and import ID. Older imports without that ID are grouped conservatively by category, version, description, and a ten minute import window. Dataset keys remain internal API values.

`GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/dir/eligible-layers` returns GeoCUP imports and per-step source requirements. `POST /dir/workflows` selects one import with the highest numeric GeoCUP version. `PUT /dir/workflows/{id}/steps/{code}` sets the old and evidence layers for a step. `POST /steps/{code}/analyze` proposes findings. `PATCH /findings/{id}` confirms matches, evidence, distance, coverage, grade, and outcome. Steps 1–6 can be skipped with a reason. `POST /dir/workflows/{id}/compile` performs mandatory Step 7 only after those steps are completed or skipped. All routes use the project owner check.

The data picker shows category, version, source file or name, layer count, and import time. It also shows the layer names in the selected final dataset and each evidence dataset. `DELETE /dir/workflows/{id}` removes that workflow, its findings, and its generated DIR layers. It leaves all selected source data in place.

The Version 3 review viewer legend shows category, version, and source layer name for the objects in the selected finding. The finding response includes the matched GeoCUP and evidence layer IDs so the viewer can resolve those names.

Stage 2 shows review counts across all result pages. Its review summary reports the total findings, pending findings, and pending alignment, manhole, and other counts. Counts update after each review or rejection.

Stage 3 offers `POST /dir/v3/workflows/{id}/stages/3/confirm-evidence` with the expected workflow revision. It checks source hashes and every pending finding's saved GeoCUP and investigation evidence before writing. If any finding is invalid, no finding changes. Otherwise it confirms all pending findings in one transaction using their saved evidence, proposed grade, and proposed coverage as validated coverage, leaves reviewed findings unchanged, and completes Stage 3. Individual review remains available.

The selected final dataset must have category `S5_GCUP`. `GET /dir/workflows/{id}/grade-summary` returns grade counts for all its records and separately for alignments. This is a completeness check, not a Grade D assignment. Step 1 accepts `S5A_CUP` sources. Analysis returns CUP source grade counts, including blank grades. `POST /dir/workflows/{id}/steps/1/confirm` requires a reviewer confirmation that ungraded selected CUP records came from data-owner service plans; only then it records study-local Grade D defaults for their feature IDs. It never changes uploaded grades. The workbook lists the final GeoCUP grade counts, CUP source counts, and each study-local Grade D default. Version 3 Stage 5 completes the grade audit even when final alignments have no source grade; the workbook lists each ungraded alignment, its baseline match, and any reviewed Stage 3 or 4 grade proposal. Proposals remain distinct from source grades.

Step 2 compares legacy manholes with surveyed covers and can record additional surveyed manholes. Step 3 compares legacy alignments with adjusted GeoCUP alignments and TOPO evidence. Steps 4, 4A, and 5 review investigation evidence and grades. Step 6 checks grades on the fixed GeoCUP import. A confirmed deviation at or above 600 mm or a confirmed missing legacy feature produces Grade E geometry. DIR geometry uses zero Z values in the Z-required database columns; DIR GDB export writes 2D geometry. The workbook includes step sources, skip reasons, reviewed evidence, and page 103 summaries. A study with all optional checks skipped gives an empty DIR and states that no accuracy assessment was performed.

## Storage

Migration `a6d1e4f8b203` adds two tables in `uuai`:

- `dir_study` stores the project, complete old and new GeoCUP layer groups, evidence layer IDs, source hashes, status, revision, and generated DIR layer IDs.
- `dir_finding` stores reviewed baseline comparisons and pending final manholes without a baseline match. It stores matched new and evidence feature IDs, the generated DIR feature ID, proposed and confirmed distances, outcome, grade, correction decision, reviewer, and revision. Only findings that produce DIR geometry reference a generated feature; multiple qualifying findings for the same original feature share that feature ID.

Generated geometry uses existing `uuai.project_layer`, `uuai.geom_line`, and `uuai.geom_polygon` rows. Its attributes use `ipag_schema.attr_dir_ext`. The generated layers use category `S6_DIR`, names `DIR_CLIN` and `DIR_NODE`, and Grade E. Generated features copy the original geometry and available owner, type, and infrastructure IDs. No input geometry or attribute is updated. A second generation replaces only the layers recorded by the same study.

## API flow

All routes require the authenticated project owner.

1. `GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/dir/eligible-layers` lists GeoCUP version groups and evidence layers. The client selects complete groups by layer ID. Numeric version order determines the default old and new choices; upload time is informational.
2. `POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/dir/studies` takes `old_layer_ids`, `new_layer_ids`, and optional `evidence_layer_ids`. The new numeric version must be greater than the old version, including dotted numbers such as `1.10` after `1.9`. The response is a study record.
3. `POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/dir/studies/{study_id}/analyze` proposes matches. Exact owner, infrastructure type, feature type, and `META_INFID` values take priority. A 10 m spatial search suggests a match when this key is absent. TOPO points and investigation lines within 2 m become suggested evidence. Suggestions do not count as reviewed results.
4. `GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/dir/studies/{study_id}/findings` returns the findings and old/new geometry for review. `PATCH /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/dir/studies/{study_id}/findings/{finding_id}` confirms links, evidence IDs, measured deviation in metres, outcome, grade, and correction decision. It requires `expected_revision` and returns 409 for a stale edit.
5. `POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/dir/studies/{study_id}/generate` requires every finding to be reviewed. It reads the `DIR_DEVIATION` threshold from `ipag_reference.validation_rule` for `R3_2026`. A confirmed deviation at or above 600 mm, or an old record confirmed missing, becomes Grade E DIR geometry. A new-only manhole appears in the report, with no old geometry to copy.
6. `GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/dir/studies/{study_id}/report.xlsx` returns the manhole and alignment summaries. The current `export-gdb` and `export-geojson` endpoints export the generated DIR layer IDs without contract changes.

Source hashes cover geometry and the fields used by the comparison. If selected data changes, analysis, review, generation, and report download return 409; create a new study. Alignment report counts and 2D lengths use distinct matched new segments and their stored GeoCUP grades. Unrepresented grades appear on an `Other grades` sheet. The manhole correction total is the sum of deviations, missing old manholes, and additional new manholes.

The frontend DIR tab in project settings selects versions and evidence, shows proposed geometry, records reviews, and downloads the report or current GIS export. The main API has no generated frontend types; the new response types are local to this panel. New FastAPI schemas appear in OpenAPI automatically. Existing IPAG semantic and export contracts are unchanged.

## Distance and decisions

Manhole distance uses centroids. Alignment distance is the maximum offset of final vertices from the original geometry. This is not a symmetric Hausdorff distance. A shorter final line lying on the original can have zero offset.

The rule comes from **DIR_DEVIATION** for **R3_2026**. The documented threshold is 600 mm. The code reads the rule at runtime; this run did not query its live value.

- **Within tolerance** is confirmed automatically.
- Certain polygon manhole matches are confirmed automatically even when deviated. They use matching infrastructure keys or strict spatial overlap.
- Other deviations remain pending. Review requires a measured distance, a matching outcome, and a correction flag for a deviation.
- The reviewer can explicitly set a new original reference. Selecting a feature alone does not save it.
- **No baseline match** sends a rejected outcome with no distance or correction. It clears the original reference, preserves a reviewed audit row, and updates missing-data counts. It creates no Grade E geometry.

Unmatched final manholes remain pending for review. Unmatched alignments and original-only features are summary counts, not new geometry findings. A rejected manhole counts as Found Additional in the report; rejected alignments do not enter its summary.

See [[Compile and exports]] for the Grade E boundary. Earlier saved analysis methods keep their older behavior until sources reset the analysis.

## Distance and decisions

Manhole distance uses centroids. Alignment distance is the maximum offset of final vertices from the original geometry. This is not a symmetric Hausdorff distance. A shorter final line lying on the original can have zero offset.

The rule comes from **DIR_DEVIATION** for **R3_2026**. The documented threshold is 600 mm. The code reads the rule at runtime; this run did not query its live value.

- **Within tolerance** is confirmed automatically.
- Certain polygon manhole matches are confirmed automatically even when deviated. They use matching infrastructure keys or strict spatial overlap.
- Other deviations remain pending. Review requires a measured distance, a matching outcome, and a correction flag for a deviation.
- The reviewer can explicitly set a new original reference. Selecting a feature alone does not save it.
- **No baseline match** sends a rejected outcome with no distance or correction. It clears the original reference, preserves a reviewed audit row, and updates missing-data counts. It creates no Grade E geometry.

Unmatched final manholes remain pending for review. Unmatched alignments and original-only features are summary counts, not new geometry findings. A rejected manhole counts as Found Additional in the report; rejected alignments do not enter its summary.

See [[Compile and exports]] for the Grade E boundary. Earlier saved analysis methods keep their older behavior until sources reset the analysis.

2. **Geometry review.** See [[Geometry review decisions]].
3. **EML and MCGPR.** Select complete S2_EML or S3_MCGPR datasets. Analyze nearby alignment evidence and proposed coverage. Review each finding or use Confirm evidence. Bulk confirmation validates all pending saved findings before writing, accepts saved proposed coverage when no validated length exists, and leaves prior reviews unchanged.
4. **Trial trench.** Select complete S4_TTR datasets. Review local trench evidence and dependent grades. B+ requires the Stage 4 check and full reviewed prior non-invasive coverage.
5. **Validate final GeoCUP.** Audit final alignment grades. Missing source grades do not block completion; the workbook lists them and reviewed proposals separately.

Every stored finding must be reviewed. Source hashes must still match.

For v3, compilation considers Stage 2 findings with an independent original baseline. It excludes generic nodes and rejected findings. The current geocup_anchor_v2 method accepts paired within-tolerance or deviated comparisons. Qualifying deviations copy distinct original baseline geometry into Grade E output. Original-only missing counts alone do not create Grade E records in this method.

Only original lines and polygons can compile. Unsupported point geometry blocks generation. The generated layers are **S6_DIR / DIR_CLIN** and **S6_DIR / DIR_NODE**. They copy available owner and infrastructure fields, store Grade E attributes, and link qualifying findings to generated features.

## Deliverables and empty output

The Excel download uses the shared **/dir/studies/{id}/report.xlsx** endpoint after generation. It includes owner manhole and alignment summaries, final grade review, workflow sources and skip reasons, reviewed evidence, and conditional sheets for missing or other grades. Report lengths use whole selected features. They are not clipped area lengths.

The current panel offers **Export DIR GIS** only when at least one generated layer ID exists. It calls the project GDB export. A separate project GeoJSON endpoint exists but is not a second button in this panel.

If all five optional stages are skipped, compilation can succeed with no output layers. The workbook explicitly says no accuracy assessment was performed. An empty output does not establish accuracy.

See [[Blocks and recovery]] for locks and failures.

It is not a hidden approval step.

- **422 during setup.** Select the highest-version final GeoCUP, a disjoint usable baseline group, confirmed original provenance, and a valid area touching final data.
- **409 before the next stage.** Complete or skip preceding stages. Pending findings keep their stage incomplete.
- **409 on review or confirmation.** Reload a stale finding or workflow revision before saving.
- **409 on changed sources.** Create a new study when a selected layer disappears or its hash changes.
- **422 during evidence review.** Select eligible unique evidence, confirm a valid measurement and outcome, and keep validated length within the alignment.
- **422 during compilation.** Resolve original point geometry; Grade E output accepts lines and polygons.
- **503 for the DIR rule.** The runtime rule is missing or invalid. This local explanation cannot verify database configuration.

## Reset, skip, and generated locks

Changing a stage's sources clears that stage's findings and resets later reviews and Stage 6. Skipping requires a reason and also resets dependent work. A generated study locks source changes and finding edits. A new study is required to change generated sources.

The delete route removes a workflow, its findings, and its generated layers while retaining source layers. This explanation did not call it.

See [[Study setup and scope]], [[Evidence and grade audit]], and [[Compile and exports]].

The six-stage plan maps the Annex C template to an audit of an already graded final GeoCUP. It preserves original geometry as the basis for Grade E DIR and separates evidence proposals from uploaded grades.

The later Stage 2 plan changes the candidate direction to final GeoCUP. The current implementation confirms that direction and records geocup_anchor_v2. Historical defect descriptions and data counts in plans are not evidence about this run. No historical customer records or identifiers are reproduced here.

## Where current code is narrower

New v3 setup requires an independent baseline group and original-provenance confirmation. Older plan language about operating without an independent baseline describes broader intent or compatibility handling, not an available new-study path.

Stage 5 audits missing grades and completes. It does not enforce complete grading as a hard compilation prerequisite. New Stage 2 original-only features are missing-data counts; they are not automatically confirmed missing legacy geometry.

## What this run checks

The editable Marmerlade workspace, native rendered views, linked documents, slide deck, imported image, Mermaid export, and native GIF are local deliverables. Their actual checks and file paths are recorded in the completion report and artifacts manifest.

Xray screens, API transactions, rule rows, migrations, reports generated from live data, and GDB conversion were not run. All Xray behavior described here is supported by source inspection, not runtime acceptance.

## Authoring context

The catalog Kiro icon identifies an authoring/tool context only. It is not part of the Xray DIR processing path. This project was authored through Marmerlade MCP in Codex. ## Distance and decisions

Manhole distance uses centroids. Alignment distance is the maximum offset of final vertices from the original geometry. This is not a symmetric Hausdorff distance. A shorter final line lying on the original can have zero offset.

The rule comes from **DIR_DEVIATION** for **R3_2026**. The documented threshold is 600 mm. The code reads the rule at runtime; this run did not query its live value.

- **Within tolerance** is confirmed automatically.
- Certain polygon manhole matches are confirmed automatically even when deviated. They use matching infrastructure keys or strict spatial overlap.
- Other deviations remain pending. Review requires a measured distance, a matching outcome, and a correction flag for a deviation.
- The reviewer can explicitly set a new original reference. Selecting a feature alone does not save it.
- **No baseline match** sends a rejected outcome with no distance or correction. It clears the original reference, preserves a reviewed audit row, and updates missing-data counts. It creates no Grade E geometry.

Unmatched final manholes remain pending for review. Unmatched alignments and original-only features are summary counts, not new geometry findings. A rejected manhole counts as Found Additional in the report; rejected alignments do not enter its summary.

See [[Compile and exports]] for the Grade E boundary. Earlier saved analysis methods keep their older behavior until sources reset the analysis.
